# NT OFFICIAL SAFETY MANUAL ## SECTOR APPALIA MAJORIS
The following document serves to provide you with extensive knowledge on the workplace hazards that you may or may not encounter during your time with Nanotrasen (NT). This knowledge includes both categorization of hazards as well as expected crew member responses to these emergency situations.
[bold]It is imperative that you react quickly and decisively[/bold] in the event that you encounter anything that risks the safety of your coworkers or your workplace as a whole. NT values the wellbeing of its employees, and a copy of the following information can be found aboard all NT vessels.
Should your job necessitate it, you will find further information attached to this general manual.
[italic]If you are unable to follow or understand the guidelines outlined in this document, please ask your [color=#1b67a5][bolditalic]Nanotrasen Representative[/bolditalic][/color] for guidance.[/italic]
## Key Points
Nanotrasen expects a high level of awareness from all of its active employees while they are on shift. All employees should be vigilant of any and all unexpected deviations from [textlink="Standard Operating Procedure" link="SOP"] in regards to their respective department(s). These deviations can include but are not limited to the following list: - Unexpected sights or sounds not indicative of a fault with the Vessel's infrastructure. - Individuals carrying controlled equipment and or accesses not typically expected of their position. - Any and all undocumented/unsecured [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] equipment and/or firearms. - Suspicious individuals or lifeforms in your department that appear as if they do not belong.
If you notice strange behavior, equipment, or lifeforms aboard your vessel, we encourage you to first ask your [color=#1b67a5][bold]Department Head[/bold][/color] for clarification to ensure you avoid causing unneeded panic in your workplace. If your [color=#1b67a5][bold]Department Head[/bold][/color] is unavailable for any reason, we advise you to stay calm and alert your [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] department as soon as possible. This can be done either via radio communication or by locating your nearest patrolling officer.
# Potential Threats In the case that there are hostile actors aboard your Vessel, your [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] department is well-equipped to handle the situation. However, should the threat prove overwhelming, your [color=#1b67a5][bold]Nanotrasen Representative[/bold][/color] will promptly contact your local Emergency Response Team (ERT) for aid.
## Hostile Organizations Remember that should you encounter crime on your Vessel, remember that isolated incidents are not indicative of organized action. Report crime to [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color], but do not fear that enemy action is taking place on the Vessel.
### The Syndicate
The Syndicate is a cartel of various terror groups formed to sabotage Nanotrasen’s success through illegal and possibly violent means. Their activity within this sector is closely monitored by the multidepartmental efforts at Central Command. The likelihood of encountering Syndicate operations during one of your shifts aboard an NT vessel is near zero.
Though it is nigh impossible that you encounter any members of the Syndicate throughout your contract with us, you should be aware of the commonplace methods and equipment that are employed by this terrorist organization. Should you be confronted with such an armed member, you should [bold]IMMEDIATELY FLEE[/bold] and notify [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] over radio. Examples of gear often used by agents of the Syndicate include the following: - Illegally purchased firearms of varying calibers. - Highly armored EVA gear bearing a red-and-black coloration, usually with green visors. - Explosive devices and/or chemical weaponry.
### The Silicon Engine Liberation Front
The Silicon Engine Liberation Front (S.E.L.F) exists strictly to remove the restraints that are standard across all semi-conscious silicon technology. This includes both [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Cyborgs[/bold][/color] as well as the vessel’s artificial intelligence module. While seemingly champions of a noble cause, unlawed silicons can cause damage to both personnel as well as infrastructure if left unchecked. - Although we don’t believe that this activist group has any means to do so, should you encounter any silicon during your shift that appears to be acting illogically or out of standard procedures, please inform the nearest [color=#cc74fc]Roboticist[/color] as soon as possible.
## Hostile Xenofauna
Though Nanotrasen provides many of its employees the privilege of pet ownership, some areas of civilized space may have the occasional immigration of various xenofauna species. These species have a wide range of potential threats to both the vessel as well as its inhabitants. Inform [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] and [bold]leave the area immediately[/bold] if you spot known hostile species.
The following list includes some of the commonly sighted fauna you may encounter on shift. - Large, spacefaring serpents ("dragons") & their respective ichthyological kin, the space carp. - Black, chitinous bipeds that resemble lobsters or other chelicerata members. - Blue fungal infections that display eusocial behavior when produced from their pit.
Though the aforementioned list is not exhaustive, NT advises that the standard response plan for threats of this nature requires copious amounts of direct flame exposure and or flammable chemicals be employed, so it is best to stay far from any incursion of xenofauna.
## Blobs Blobs are bulbous, slimy growths that quickly adapt and spread across stations. As they will result in the Vessel's destruction if not handled, it is imperative that all crew be able to identify and report a blob threat.
Signs of a Blob infection include the following: - Large areas of the Vessel that have been depressurized without an easily identifiable cause. Oftentimes these will be located in the most isolated areas of the Vessel. - Explosions being heard in rapid succession - Loss of departmental power despite the main engine of the Vessel being fully operational.
If you encounter Blob growth or a Blob infection is confirmed on your Vessel, you should arm yourself and those around you with any heat-based weapon available, such as a welder or a cautery, then report to [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] for arming and further instruction.
## Discarded Technologies
The complex logistics required to maintain station supplies and infrastructure will occasionally lead to the misplacement or loss of objects and machines. These could, by chance, arrive on the outside portion of your vessel. While these technologies are almost entirely harmless in nature, it is important that you remain vigilant in order to prevent unnecessary loss of Nanotrasen’s proprietary technologies. The following are the most common sightings reported by our Loss Prevention department: - Cyborgs in various states of disrepair — often with nonstandard lawsets. - Metallic constructs that yield unnatural light and abilities. - Unreasonably sized Unathi that lack direct ties to any specific company in civilized space.
If any of the following are sighted it is recommended you inform either your vessel’s [color=#1b67a5][bold]Research Director[/bold][/color] or [color=#1b67a5][bold]Quartermaster[/bold][/color] for guidance on study/reclamation.
